title: High-NA EUV productivity complicates die height design
author: Xebec
text:
F

Fred Chen
Moderator

The number of row scans in a 33 mm height affects the productivity of High-NA scanners. This was shown at 2023 IMEC Technology Forum (ITF). This, in turn, depends on die height. The best case is when an even number of rows fits within 33 mm. However, at other die heights, the productivity drops at least 10%, and in some cases, stitching is required. Narrow die height bins result. For more than 16.5 mm, stitching is always required.

The 12" mask size definitely cannot come soon enough, but for current users (i.e., Intel), die height will have to be a design target. Also, DRAM users are heading toward 6 mm die height, so stitching is already a big complication from using High-NA.
